root_cause.text: The driver prematurely frees the as102_dev_t structure in the error path after a successful usb_register_dev() call, while existing open file descriptors can still access and free the same memory via .release(), causing a use-after-free and double-free race condition.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description and commit message detail the race: CPU0 probes, calls usb_register_dev(), then on an error path does usb_deregister_dev() and kfree(as102_dev_t) immediately; meanwhile CPU1 has opened the device and later closes it, triggering as102_release() → as102_usb_release() which also kfree()s the same structure. The patch removes the kfree() from the failed_stream error path and returns directly, deferring memory deallocation to the release callback.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix error handling in as102_usb_probe to prevent double put_device and ensure proper cleanup ordering in the failed_stream error path.
intent_record.what: In the failed_stream error path of as102_usb_probe, added usb_set_intfdata(intf, NULL) before usb_deregister_dev and added a return ret; statement to prevent fall-through to the failed label.
intent_record.how: This ensures the interface driver data is cleared before deregistration and that the function returns early with an error code instead of continuing to the failed label, avoiding a double call to usb_put_dev and redundant operations.

candidates.rationale: This statement prematurely decrements the reference count on the USB device after usb_register_dev() succeeded. If this is the last reference, it frees the USB device, which likely contains or is closely associated with the as102_dev_t structure. Existing open file descriptors can still access and free the same memory via .release(), leading to a use-after-free and double-free race condition.
